parsed.summary: This paper evaluates the feasibility of using quadruped robots, specifically the Unitree Go2, for automated tasks in roof environments. Using a custom-built test rig with standard roof tiles, the authors found that standard ball feet are inadequate for sloped roofs, with slippage increasing quadratically and critical failures occurring regularly at a 25-degree incline. The study concludes that safe roof locomotion will require a combination of terrain-aware control strategies and customized foot designs.

chk_problem.value: Investigating the feasibility of using quadruped walking robots to automate hazardous and repetitive construction and maintenance tasks in roof environments.
chk_problem.paper_quote: This paper investigates the feasibility of deploying quadruped walking robots for the automation of work in roof environments.

chk_method.value: Designing a dedicated roof surface test rig to evaluate the baseline performance of a commercial Unitree Go2 quadruped robot.
chk_method.paper_quote: A dedicated test rig of a roof’s surface was designed to evaluate the baseline performance of a commercial quadruped, the Unitree Go2, in this new environment.

chk_data.value: The Frankfurter Pfanne roof tiles, which are the most common type of roof tile in Germany, used as the surface material on the test rig.
chk_data.paper_quote: As surface material the Frankfurther Pfanne was chosen, which is the most common type of roof tile in Germany [2].

chk_setup.value: Evaluating the robot's balancing, get-up/lie-down sequences, and incline walking on the test rig, with trials controlled via Python at 1.0 m/s.
chk_setup.paper_quote: With the Go2, three core skills were examined: balancing on continuously increasing inclines, get-up/lie-down sequences, and incline walking.

chk_primary_result.value: Slippage increased quadratically with incline angle, and critical failures occurred regularly on moderate inclines of 25°.
chk_primary_result.paper_quote: Experiments revealed that standard ball feet are inherently inadequate for locomotion on sloped roofs: slippage increased quadratically with incline angle, get-up and lie-down sequences were only possible on small inclines, and critical failures already occurred regularly on moderate inclines of 25◦ .

chk_secondary_result.value: The critical angle for standing on an incline was measured at 27.58 ± 0.72° on average, and get-up/lie-down sequences succeeded only up to 11°.
chk_secondary_result.paper_quote: For standing on an incline, the critical angle was measured at (27.58 ± 0.72)◦ on average.

chk_baseline.value: The robot's performance was compared against the manufacturer's claims of slope-climbing capabilities of up to 40°.
chk_baseline.paper_quote: Manufacturer claims of slopeclimbing capabilities of up to 40◦ were not achieved under the test conditions [18].

chk_conclusion.value: Unmodified quadrupeds are currently not capable of safe and reliable operation in roof environments.
chk_conclusion.paper_quote: These results underscore that, without appropriate adaptations, quadrupeds are not yet capable of safe and reliable operation in roof environments.

chk_limitation.value: The experiments were conducted under ideal conditions without any debris, vegetation, weather, or additional payloads.
chk_limitation.paper_quote: Lastly, all experiments have been conducted under ideal conditions, no additional debris, vegetation, weather or additional payloads were added.
